data.long_meaning: Dhir is a Sanskrit word that originates from the root 'dhri' meaning to uphold, sustain, or hold. The name Dhir signifies intelligence, understanding, and wisdom. It is believed to be an auspicious name for a boy, reflecting the qualities of a wise and intelligent leader. The name Dhir carries the meaning “Intelligence, understanding” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dhir usually hope their child will grow to embody intelligence, understanding and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dhir total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Dhir, derived from the Sanskrit word 'dhira', means 'wise' or 'serene'. It symbolizes one who possesses inner strength, calmness, and deep understanding. In Hinduism, this name is often associated with sages and seekers of enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Dhira Saraswati, also known as Matsyendranath, was a revered Hindu sage and one of the founders of Tantra. He is believed to have lived between the 8th and 11th centuries CE. Matsyendranath is considered the guru of Gorakhnath, the founder of the Nath tradition of yoga and Tantra.

Dhira Gupta was a prominent Hindu king of the Pala Empire in Bengal during the late 11th and early 12th centuries CE. He was known for his military exploits and his patronage of art and culture, particularly in the temple town of Bhubaneswar.
